transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Mistral CTO), Aisha Khan (Lead Platform Eng), Ben Turner (Product)

Summary (auto): quick SDK walkthrough, auth patterns, env setup, next steps to run POC and share security docs.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our SE, we'll run through the SDK quickstarts and auth patterns and then leave time for your environment questions.
[00:20] Carlos: hey thanks, excited — we want to see how fast we can get inference calls from our services, mostly node and python microservices on EKS, and we have strict SSO/compliance requirements.
[00:35] Priya: great, we'll start with the quickstart, show python and ts examples, then the console and network/auth considerations. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:50] Ben: quick ask — cost/latency profile? we care about tail latency for realtime checkout flows.
[01:10] Priya: noted; we'll point out batching, model choices, and routing to Dedicated vs Hosted later — for the quickstart we'll use the hosted API to get you going quickly.

--- Quickstart walkthrough ---
[03:15] Priya: Ok first the Python snippet, super minimal, sets REDWOOD_API_KEY in env. Example: 
python snippet: 
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate('Summarize order 12345')
print(resp.text)

[04:05] Aisha: are there official packages? we run pipenv/poetry.
[04:18] Jordan: yes we publish on PyPI and npm, versions pinned in quickstart, we also have dockerized examples for CI.
[04:30] Priya: TypeScript example: 
import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.generate('short summary')
console.log(resp.text)

[05:10] Carlos: ok so API key in env, but we use internal IDP — how do teams authenticate server-to-server?
[05:25] Priya: common patterns: 1) server app stores Redwood API key in secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, KMS) and injects into env at runtime. 2) For orgs with SSO and tighter security, we offer Private deployment and SSO integration (SAML/OIDC) to manage keys via RBAC and provisioned service principals. 3) You can also use short-lived tokens via our token exchange if you want ephemeral creds.

[06:00] Ben: do you support automatic token rotation?
[06:10] Jordan: yes, we recommend rotating via your secrets manager; Redwood's CLI/console can rotate service keys and we log key usage in audit logs.

--- Console demo & env setup ---
[07:40] Priya: switching to the console — quick look at API keys page, how to create keys, scopes (generate/chat/embeddings), and per-route quotas. Also we have per-token cost breakdown on the usage view.
[09:00] Aisha: we have a proxy that blocks external egress except to allowlisted endpoints, can we run in a Private mode?
[09:18] Priya: yes two options: 1) Private (VPC-managed) where Redwood control plane runs in your VPC or 2) On-prem package where everything is customer-hosted. For immediate POC you can use hosted but you'll need to allow egress to Redwood endpoints or use a NAT gateway with allowlist. We can share IP ranges and FQDNs.
[09:50] Carlos: we also need to keep logs inside our environment for compliance, is that possible?
[10:05] Jordan: for Dedicated/Private customers, logs/audit can be shipped to your SIEM or kept inside your VPC. Hosted customers get audit logs in the console but we can arrange SOC2 artifacts and retention packs. We'll send the security pack after this call.

--- Auth deep dive & network ---
[12:30] Priya: about SSO — we integrate with SAML and OIDC providers. For service accounts we recommend provisioning an identity and binding via RBAC to only the scopes needed. If you need KMS-backed keys we support BYOK integration with common KMS providers.
[13:20] Aisha: our KMS is AWS KMS and we have HSM-backed keys for some flows. Any blockers?
[13:35] Priya: no blockers; for Private deployments we can enable BYOK so keys never leave your KMS. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys via an HSM integration for enterprise tiers.

--- Code / deployment patterns ---
[15:00] Priya: recommended pattern for EKS: 1) store REDWOOD_API_KEY in SecretsManager or as Kubernetes secret (sealed secret), 2) sidecar proxy approach if you want retries/observability, 3) use non-blocking async calls or streaming for long responses.
[16:10] Ben: how do we handle retries and idempotency?
[16:20] Priya: Redwood SDK has idempotency tokens for generate calls and a retry policy built-in; we suggest exponential backoff and logging tokens for tracing.

[18:05] Carlos: can we do local dev without sending data to Redwood? dev environment constraints.
[18:20] Jordan: yes, we publish mocked SDK mode and a local simulator image for offline dev. You can flip to real keys for staging. We'll include that in the quickstart repo.

--- POC/Benchmark discussion ---
[20:30] Priya: POC suggestion: run two endpoints — a 512-token chat and a 128-token embedding workload, measure P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. We'll provide a benchmark harness and sample scripts.
[21:10] Aisha: we have a load testing cluster, we can run that provided we get the API endpoint and a test key. What's typical throughput on hosted?
[21:25] Priya: depends on model and batch size; we'll propose a config. If you need guaranteed throughput, Dedicated is the route. For POC hosted is fine.

[22:40] Ben: any blockers around data residency? we're EU customers with some EU-only data.
[22:50] Jordan: we have region controls and can route requests to EU regions; Private deploy is for full data residency. We'll document region support for the models.

--- Objections & tradeoffs ---
[25:10] Carlos: worried about vendor lock-in and portability.
[25:25] Priya: portable model formats and exportable KV caches are supported; we give model version pins and you can bring your own model variants in Private deployments. We'll show how to pin models in the config.

[27:00] Aisha: cost visibility — we need per-route token breakdown and alerts.
[27:12] Jordan: Console has per-route cost, token-level breakdowns, and you can set alerts. Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quantization to reduce unit costs.

--- Wrap and next steps ---
[30:05] Jordan: quick recap — we'll send quickstart repo, security pack (SOC2, network ranges, KMS options), and a sample benchmark harness. Suggested next meeting: POC kickoff week of 6/22.
[30:25] Carlos: sounds good, can Priya run the benchmark config with our test key?
[30:35] Priya: yes we'll coordinate, I'll need SSO/IDP details only if you want Private or SSO-bound keys, otherwise a service key is fine.
[31:00] Ben: timeline — target MVP by end of July, POC to validate latency and cost by mid-June.
[31:20] Jordan: noted. We'll action items and share links.

[31:40] Priya: small gotchas — remember streaming changes client behavior, and batching can increase tail latency if not tuned. We'll include recommended defaults for checkout flows.
[32:10] Aisha: please include our proxy allowlist details in the docs.
[32:20] Jordan: will do.

[35:00] Carlos: one more security question — do you support FIPS endpoints?
[35:12] Jordan: FIPS/HSM are available for enterprise Private deployments; for hosted we'll check current FIPS coverage and include in the security pack.

[37:30] Priya: demo over, open Qs?
[37:45] Ben: nothing else.
[38:00] Aisha: we'll gather IDP config and send it to Jordan.
[38:15] Carlos: thanks team this helped clarify path forward.
[38:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule POC kickoff.
